values of 1 to 5 corresponding to each philosopher that is P 1 P 2 P 3 P 4 of P 5. Now, in the function
we have an infinite loop where the i th philosopher will think for some time and then after some time
he begins to feel hungry. So, he will take the fox on his right then take the fox on his left
then he is going to eat for some time and after that he is going to put down the left fox
and then put down the right fox and this continues in a loop infinitely. So, for instance philosophy
for P 1 would think for some time then he will hungry then he would pick up the right fox that is
the fox number 1 then pick up the left fox that is fox 2 then eat for some time and put down the
fox first 2 and then 1. So, this seems like a very simple and easy solution to the problem
but as you will see that there are certain issues that can could crop up.
The issues come because each of these philosophers which essentially executes this function
independently or thinking and feeling hungry and eating all independently.
So, let us consider this particular scenario. Let us say the philosophers P 1 and P 3 have a
higher priority that is whenever they request for the fox to be picked up then the system will
always ensure that they are given the fox. So, what would happen in such a case? So, we will
get us case where P 1 eats whenever he wants and P 3 eats whenever he wants while the other
philosophers P 2 P 4 and P 5 which have the lower priority in picking the fox will not be able to
eat. For instance the philosopher P 2 neither could pick up the right fork or the left fork
and therefore, P 2 cannot eat. In a similar manner P 4 and P 5 have just one fork between them which
they could possibly pick up. The other fork in each case would with high probability be given to
the philosophers P 1 and P 3 thus P 2 P 4 and P 5 will starve and this is not the ideal solution
for our problem. So, let us see another possible issue that could take place.
So, let us say by some chance all the philosophers pick up their right fork simultaneously. So,
we have a philosopher P 1 picking up his right fork philosopher P 2 picking the right fork
of P 3 P 4 P 5 pick up their right fork respectively. Now, in order to eat each of the philosophers
have to pick up their left fork and this could lead to a starvation. Essentially P 1 is waiting

chain and this waiting will go on infinitely leaving leading to starvation which we often call
